care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

You live in the UK.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)

  - No other claimant who lives with the child has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Claimant and another person are both responsible for the child and cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help determine your eligibility, I need to understand your situation. 

First, let me ask about the child or children you're claiming for:

**Do you have a child (or children) that you're responsible for?** If yes, please tell me:
- The child's name
- Their age (or date of birth)

The age of the child is important because:
- Children **under 16** automatically qualify
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **20 or over** generally don't qualify

Please share the details about your child or children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm responsible for my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're responsible for Alex, who is 15 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, he automatically meets the age requirement for Child Benefit. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to check Alex's work status:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

At 15 years old, this is typically straightforward, but I need to confirm whether Alex:
- Is not working at all, OR
- Works less than 24 hours per week

What's Alex's current work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all. He's still in school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is still in school and not working, so that's fine.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to confirm that Alex is not currently receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

...in their own name (not as part of your household claim).

At 15 years old and in school, this is typically not the case, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship?**

If not, that's fine. If yes, I need to know:
- What type of apprenticeship
- Which country (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)

This matters because:
- Most apprenticeships (in England and Scotland) disqualify from Child Benefit
- Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales are the exception and ARE approved

Since Alex is 15 and in school, I'm assuming he's not in an apprenticeship, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing an apprenticeship. He's just in regular school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in regular school, so that's all good. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status, as the claimant must meet UK residency requirements.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

This is usually straightforward - if you live in the UK as your main home, you'll meet this requirement. 

However, if you don't normally live in the UK, there are some special circumstances that might still qualify you, such as:
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Being a Crown servant living abroad
- Other specific situations

So, do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives at home with you, which means you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. You're considered responsible if you either:
- Live with the child (which you do), OR
- Contribute to their upkeep at least the amount of Child Benefit

Since Alex lives with you, this is satisfied. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative or guardian
- Anyone else

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. If someone else is already claiming, you would need to agree on who should claim before proceeding.

Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You mentioned he lives at home with you, but I need to confirm:

**Is Alex currently:**
- In hospital?
- In local authority care?
- Being fostered?
- Or living normally at home with you?

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you. Can you confirm that's correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me full-time. He's not in hospital, care, or being fostered.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you (not the local council) responsible for covering Alex's living costs and support?

Since Alex lives with you at home and you're supporting him, I'm assuming the council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm covering all his living costs myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex is 15 years old** - under 16, so automatically qualifies  
✅ **Not working** - he's in regular school  
✅ **Not receiving benefits** - no ESA or Universal Credit in his own name  
✅ **Not in an apprenticeship** - attending regular school  
✅ **You meet UK residency requirements** - you normally live in the UK  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - he lives with you and you support him  
✅ **No competing claims** - no one else is claiming for Alex  
✅ **Living at home normally** - not in hospital, care, or fostered  
✅ **No council support** - you're covering all his living costs  

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### Important Information:

⚠️ **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay a tax charge. You can still claim but may want to discuss this with HMRC.

💷 **Payments**: Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

📋 **How to claim**: Visit https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about claiming or the process?
